question.text: What will Adama Barrow’s margin be over his highest vote-getting opponent in the 2026 Gambian presidential election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the difference, in percentage points, between President Adama Barrow's vote share and the vote share of his highest vote-getting opponent, according to official results or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), in the [2026 Gambian presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Gambian_presidential_election).
question.fine_print: If none of the other options resolve before January 1, 2027 (for example because the election is postponed or Barrow leaves the race) the question resolves as **Other result**.

research:
I could not find any result, poll or market that settles the question. The election is on 5 December 2026 and no votes have been counted. Barrow won by 25.5 points in 2021. The only 2026 poll puts his lead at 7 points before undecided voters are taken out, and that poll's methods have been criticised.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-13: The Wikipedia page for the 2026 Gambian presidential election shows no results. It gives the election date as 5 December 2026. Its candidate list is out of date: it still includes Bakary K. Badjie, whose nomination is pending, and Mohamed Al Amin Bah, and it leaves out Touray and Sima. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Gambian_presidential_election)
- The official numbers will come from the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC). In past elections results were announced within about 1 to 2 days of the vote.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The campaign has not started.
- 2026-11-12: The IEC confirmed five candidates:
  - Adama Barrow (NPP)
  - Ousainou Darboe (UDP)
  - Talib Ahmed Bensouda (UNITE)
  - Dr. Isatou Touray (independent)
  - Modou Lamin Sima (APC)
- The IEC rejected two nominations: Bakusa Dukureh (Gambia Labour Party) and Kebba Bojang (NDP). Six more, including Bakary K. Badjie, are waiting on missing documents. [Kerr Fatou](https://www.kerrfatou.com/iec-confirms-five-presidential-candidates-rejects-two-nominations-ahead-of-december-election/)
- 2026-11-12: The two-week campaign starts around 16 November. Africanews notes the IEC received 18 nomination requests. [Africanews](https://www.africanews.com/2026/11/12/the-gambias-electoral-commission-announces-5-candidates-for-presidential-poll/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-11: Darboe, 78, confirmed he is running for the UDP. RFI calls it his sixth presidential bid. [RFI](https://www.rfi.fr/ha/afrika/20261111-jagoran-adawar-gambia-ya-sanar-da-takararsa-a-za%C9%93en-shugaban-%C6%99asa)
- 2026-11-11: The government launched validation of a $60m public employment programme, which is pre-election spending. [bne IntelliNews](https://www.intellinews.com/gambia-begins-validating-proposed-public-employment-programme-484179/)
- 2026-11-10: Barrow filed for a third term, going back on his earlier pledge to serve one term only. [AA](https://www.aa.com.tr/fr/afrique/gambie-adama-barrow-candidat-%C3%A0-un-troisi%C3%A8me-mandat/4121291)
- Around 2026-11: Bensouda stepped down as mayor of Kanifing to run. [Africanews](https://www.africanews.com/2026/11/12/the-gambias-electoral-commission-announces-5-candidates-for-presidential-poll/)
- 2026-10-17: Endorsements and opposition split, per the Timbuktu Institute:
  - Essa Faal (APP-Sobeyaa) allied with Barrow and is not running.
  - Mama Kandeh joined the NPP in late July.
  - The opposition is split between Darboe's "Gambia First" and Bensouda's "Coalition 2026". Talks on a joint candidate stalled over who would lead.
  - About 20 NPP officials defected to Kebba Bojang's NDP. Bojang's own candidacy has since been rejected.
  - [Timbuktu Institute](https://timbuktu-institute.org/index.php/toutes-l-actualites/item/1817-the-gambia-barrow-piles-up-endorsements-as-the-opposition-divides)

### 4. Base rates
- 2021: Barrow 53.2%, Darboe 27.7%, a margin of about 25.5 points. Mama Kandeh came third with about 12% and Essa Faal fourth with about 6%. Both now back Barrow. [Wikipedia 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Gambian_presidential_election)
- 2016: Barrow, as the opposition coalition candidate, got about 43.3% against Jammeh's about 39.6%, a margin of about 3.7 points.
- Earlier incumbent margins under Jammeh were large: about 72% against Darboe's about 17% in 2011, and about 67% against about 27% in 2006.
- Gambia uses first-past-the-post with no runoff, so a split opposition helps the leader.
- Polls (the only ones I found, both from Gambia Participates/CepRass with 1,556 respondents each):
  - 2026-08 (reported 2026-08-21): Barrow 32%, Darboe 25%, Bensouda 19%, Faal 3%, Kandeh 2%, others 2%, undecided 17%. Raw lead: 7 points. [Gambiana](https://gambiana.com/essa-faal-records-3-support-in-latest-gambia-participates-poll/)
  - My arithmetic on the August poll: leaving out undecided voters gives about 38.6 / 30.1 / 22.9, a lead of about 8.5 points. If Faal's and Kandeh's shares also go to Barrow, the lead is about 14.5 points.
  - July 2025 CepRass: Barrow 31%, Bensouda 18%, Darboe 12%, undecided 29%. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Gambian_presidential_election)
- DataEd says the Gambia Participates poll is flawed, citing errors in method and arithmetic, and parties have disputed its findings. [The Standard](https://standard.gm/how-a-flawed-polls-threatened-to-mislead-gambias-2026-elections), [The Point](https://thepoint.gm/africa/gambia/headlines/parties-dispute-polls-finding-that-puts-barrow-ahead-of-dec-election)
- The same survey found 55% think Barrow should not seek a third term and 60% said they would not vote for him. [The Standard](https://standard.gm/survey-says-majority-of-gambians-dont-want-third-term-for-barrow-but-projects-him-likely-winner-in-2026)
- Gambian polling has little track record, so how accurate these polls are is unknown.

### 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-11-13: Kalshi, winner market: Barrow 78%, Darboe 17%, Bensouda 4%. The Faal and Kandeh contracts are about 5% each, which is stale since neither is running.
- 2026-11-13: Polymarket, winner market: Barrow 78.5%, Darboe 18.5%, Badjie 1.65%, Bensouda 1.05%.
- These are winner markets, not margin markets. Darboe is priced as the main challenger, ahead of Bensouda.
- Kalshi, 2027 parliamentary election: NPP 58%, UDP 25%, UNITE 11%.
- I found no market or expert forecast on the margin itself.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around 2026-11-16 to early December: the campaign period.
- The IEC still has to decide on the six pending nominations, including Badjie. Badjie could draw votes in Foni, the former Jammeh base.
- Any last-minute opposition deal between Darboe and Bensouda would matter, though it looks unlikely now that both are confirmed candidates.
- Any new polls during the campaign.
- 2026-12-05: polling day. Official results are expected 6 to 7 December, right around when the question resolves.
- If the result is postponed or disputed past 2026-12-31, the question resolves as "Other result".

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-13: The question resolves on official results from the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) or credible sources. The Wikipedia page shows no results yet. It says the vote is on 5 December 2026, a single round decided by plurality. Its candidate table looks out of date: it lists Badjie, Bah, Darboe, Bensouda and Barrow, not the final IEC list. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Gambian_presidential_election)
- Gambia normally announces results quickly. In 2021 the vote was on 4 December and the result was declared the next day. That is from my background knowledge, not checked today.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. Voting is on 2026-12-05.
- 2026-11-12: The IEC confirmed 5 candidates out of 18 nomination requests: Barrow (NPP), Darboe (UDP), Talib Bensouda (Unite), Isatou Touray, and Modou Lamin Sima (APC). ## 4. Base rates
Past margins between the winner and the runner-up:
- 2021: Barrow 53.23%, Darboe 27.72%, Kandeh 12.32%. Margin **25.5 points**. Kandeh (now with the NPP) and Faal (now allied) ran against Barrow then. [Wikipedia 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Gambian_presidential_election)
- 2016: Barrow, as a united opposition coalition candidate, about 43.3%, Jammeh about 39.6%. Margin **about 3.7 points**. This is from memory, not checked today.
- 2006 and 2011: Jammeh beat Darboe by about 40 and about 54 points. From memory; that was under an authoritarian incumbent.

Polls (both had a sample of 1,556; methodology disputed by parties and analysts):
- Gambia Participates, 10 Aug 2026: Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, others 7, undecided 17. Lead **7 points**.
- CepRass, July 2025: Barrow 31, Bensouda 18, Darboe 12, undecided 29. Lead **13 points**. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Gambian_presidential_election); [The Standard critique](https://standard.gm/how-a-flawed-polls-threatened-to-mislead-gambias-2026-elections)

Other points:
- If undecided voters are dropped, the Aug 2026 poll gives roughly Barrow 39, Darboe 30, a lead of about 8 to 9 points. That is my own calculation.
- Kandeh's 12% from 2021 and Faal's vote now sit with Barrow, which could push his share up compared with the poll.
- One survey found 60% would not vote for Barrow if he ran. [The Standard](https://standard.gm/survey-says-majority-of-gambians-dont-want-third-term-for-barrow-but-projects-him-likely-winner-in-2026)
- I found no poll from October or November 2026.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-11-13, Kalshi winner market: Barrow 0.78, Darboe 0.17, Bensouda 0.04. Kandeh and Faal are still listed at about 0.05 each even though they are not running, so the prices may be stale or the market thin.
- 2026-11-13, Polymarket winner market: Barrow 0.785, Darboe 0.185, Bensouda 0.0105, Badjie 0.0165.
- These are winner markets, not margin markets. I found no market or expert forecast on the margin.
- Kalshi parliamentary winner (2027): NPP 0.58, UDP 0.25, UNITE 0.11.
- The Standard ran an analysis of each candidate's path to victory, but I did not fetch it. [The Standard](https://standard.gm/barrow-darboe-and-bensouda-the-paths-to-victory-in-the-gambias-2026-presidential-election/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-16 to about 2026-11-30 (Africanews says two weeks; the end date is my inference): the official campaign. Watch rally turnout, any late opposition deal between Darboe and Bensouda (which would narrow the margin), further defections, and anything more on the Bensouda allegations.
- 2026-12-05: polling day. Results are expected around 6 or 7 December, about when the question resolves.
- After the vote, possible challenges to the results. Only a delay past 2027-01-01 would trigger "Other result".

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** Polling day is 5 December 2026, about 22 days away. Official IEC results have historically come within 1 to 2 days, so the outcome should be known around 6 to 7 December.

**(b) Status quo:** Barrow is the incumbent, and the opposition is split between Darboe (UDP) and Bensouda (UNITE). The 2021 alignment, plus Kandeh's and Faal's support moving to Barrow, points to a comfortable Barrow win. That probably means a margin in the double digits.

**(c) Base rates:**
- Gambian incumbents have won every election except 2016, when a united opposition coalition beat Jammeh by 3.7 points.
- Incumbent margins: 2006 about 40 points, 2011 about 55 points, 2021 about 25.5 points.
- Across African incumbents facing a fragmented opposition in first-past-the-post systems, margins above 20 points are common.
- The 2021 result came with Kandeh (about 12%) and Faal (about 6%) running against Barrow. Both now back him.

**(d) Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-11-13: Kalshi gives Barrow a 78% chance of winning and Polymarket 78.5%. That implies roughly a 20% chance his margin is 0 or less.
- 2026-08: The Gambia Participates/CepRass poll has Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, with 17% undecided. That is a raw lead of 7 points, or about 8.5 points once undecided voters are excluded. The poll's methods have been criticised.
- 2026-11-12: The IEC confirmed only five candidates, with the opposition divided. Darboe is 78 and on his sixth bid. Bensouda draws from a similar urban and UDP-leaning base, so a closer race for second place widens Barrow's lead.
- Against Barrow: he broke his one-term pledge, the survey found 55% oppose a third term, and about 20 NPP officials defected.
- For Barrow: the $60m employment programme is pre-election spending that helps him.

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** Third-term anger and economic discontent push opposition voters to rally tactically behind Darboe late in the campaign. Darboe then edges Barrow in a close race. Alternatively, a disputed result or a delay past the deadline produces "Other result".

**Reasoning:** I started from the incumbency base rate and the 2021 margin of 25.5 points, which would put most weight on "20 points or more". I moved down because of:
- the polls showing a single-digit lead;
- the third-term backlash;
- the market's roughly 20% chance of a Barrow loss, which I treat as an anchor for the "0 points or less" option.

The split opposition keeps substantial weight on the 10 to 20 point and 20+ point options. I left a small amount on "Other result" for postponement or a dispute.

Option_A: 0.16
Option_B: 0.21
Option_C: 0.27
Option_D: 0.32
Option_E: 0.04

(a) **Time left:** Polling day is 5 December 2026. The IEC has historically announced results within 1 to 2 days, so the outcome should be known around 6 or 7 December, about three and a half weeks from now.

(b) **Status quo:** If nothing changed, Barrow would win comfortably as incumbent. He has absorbed the 2021 third- and fourth-place finishers (Kandeh and Faal), and the opposition is split between Darboe and Bensouda under first-past-the-post. A rerun of 2021 with those additions would point to a margin of 20 points or more.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Incumbent wins in the Gambia have usually been landslides:
  - Jammeh won by about 55 points in 2011 and about 40 in 2006.
  - Barrow won by about 25.5 points in 2021.
- The one incumbent loss, Jammeh in 2016, came against a united opposition coalition and had a 3.7-point margin.
- African incumbents facing a split opposition mostly win by double digits.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **Barrow's coalition grew.** Kandeh joined the NPP in July 2026 and Faal allied with Barrow (Timbuktu Institute, 17 October 2026). In 2021 they had about 18% combined.
- **The opposition is split.** Darboe and Bensouda are both confirmed candidates (IEC, 12 November 2026), and talks on a joint candidate stalled.
- **The only poll suggests a narrower race.** The August 2026 Gambia Participates poll had Barrow 32, Darboe 25, Bensouda 19, undecided 17, a raw lead of 7 points. Leaving out undecided voters gives a lead of about 8.5 points, or about 14.5 if Faal's and Kandeh's supporters move to Barrow. The poll's methods have been criticised.
- **Barrow is vulnerable on the third term.** In the same survey, 55% opposed a third term and 60% said they would not vote for him.
- **Markets (13 November 2026)** give Barrow about 78% to win on both Kalshi and Polymarket. That implies roughly 20 to 22% that he loses, which corresponds to a margin of 0 points or less. Thin markets on obscure elections often overprice upsets, so I shade this somewhat lower.

(e) **Unexpected-outcome scenario:** Anger at the broken one-term pledge and economic hardship drives urban and young voters toward Bensouda. Darboe holds the UDP base, and turnout in NPP areas is soft. Barrow wins with only about 40%, a single-digit margin, or narrowly loses to Darboe. Alternatively, a disputed count or postponement pushes official results past the deadline, which would resolve as "Other result."

**How I got here:** The base rate alone would put about 50% on a margin of 20 points or more. I moved down for the poll and the third-term discontent. I added weight to a Barrow loss to partly respect the market's roughly 22% implied chance of defeat. The 10 to 20 point band is a natural middle outcome: Barrow at about 48 to 50% against Darboe at about 30%.

Option_A: 0.16
Option_B: 0.21
Option_C: 0.28
Option_D: 0.32
Option_E: 0.03

(a) **Time left:** Polling day is 5 December 2026, about 3 weeks away. The IEC has historically announced official results within 1 to 2 days, so the outcome should be known around 6 to 7 December, well before the 1 January 2027 cutoff.

(b) **Status quo:** Barrow is the incumbent. He has new endorsements from Kandeh and Faal, who together took about 18% in 2021, and he faces an opposition split between Darboe and Bensouda in a first-past-the-post race with no runoff.
